description_en: While a legend credits a cowherder (gvāḥor Gopālī) woman for the construction of this temple, an inscription here confirms that the Brahmāyaṇī temple already existed in the 17th century.The two-tiered Brahmāyaṇī temple in Thecva's Kvaylāchi Ṭola faces south. Clad in copper sheets on both levels, the temple culminates in a gilded finial. An elongated banner (patāḥ) hangs from the finial, reaching down to the lower roof. The first floor enshrines a gilded statue of Brahmāyaṇī. While the southern wing of the ground floor opens into seven bays, resembling aphalcā, the northern wing accommodates Gaṇeśa statues within a small room to the east of the entrance. Among these statues, the aniconic one (THC0030-003) stands as the principal Gaṇeśa, also being the oldest. A more recent statue, discovered by a local during a firewood expedition in the nearby jungle, is also enshrined here. Local folklore recounts that the discoverer, having received a divine vision of Gaṇeśa, personally carried the statue to its current resting place within the temple. A stone pillar adorned with a swan statue graces the temple's forecourt. A raised platform south of the pillar serves as a resting point for Brahmāyaṇī's palanquin during the annual procession. The masked dance of Navadurgā of Thecva is also performed on this platform. A separate shrine dedicated to Nāsaḥdyaḥ is located east of the temple.No concrete historical records exist regarding the construction of the temple; however, inscriptions verify that it was already built during the medieval period. According to legend, the temple was constructed by a cowherdess. Due to a feud among three cowherdess sisters, one established a Gaṇeśa shrine known as Gvāḥdyaḥ, another built the Brahmāyaṇī temple, and the third established a Gaṇeśa shrine at Gvāḥnani. Another version of the legend states that the elder cowherdess sister established Brahmāyaṇī in Kvaylāchi, while the younger sister established Bālakumārī in Cvaylāchi.In 1636 CE (NS 756), a group led by Kulasiṃha constructed a dance platform in Thecva. As the inscription is set in the temple wall, the platform mentioned here probably refers to the one in front of the temple. In 1702 CE (NS 823), the seniors of Thecva, Bhārasiṃha Bhābo and Sūrya Bhābo, established a Gaṇeśa statue (THC0030-002). In 1717 CE (NS 837), a guild dedicated to chanting Buddhist hymns in Thecva paved the open space in front of the Brahmāyaṇī temple with floor tiles. In the same year, Gumīsiṃha Bhābo, Dātemha Bhābo, Indrasiṃ Bhābo, and others collectively donated three woodentoraṇas for Brahmāyaṇī. In 1901 CE (NS 1021), the old wooden pillar in front of the Brahmāyaṇī temple was replaced with a stone pillar.As the 2015 Nepal earthquakes damaged the temple, the Department of Archaeology decided to rebuild the temple. In 2017 CE (VS 2073), the temple was dismantled and the Brahmāyaṇī statue was temporarily relocated to thesataḥwest of the temple. However, the statue was stolen on January 3, 2018 while it was placed in thesataḥ(local resident, Maharjana, male, age 38). This was not the first incident of theft; the Brahmāyaṇī statue had been stolen twice before. Unfortunately, none of the stolen statues have been recovered. Consequently, the locals collectively installed a new statue on each occasion. This is the fourth Brahmāyaṇī statue to be installed in the temple. Following the completion of the temple’s reconstruction, the Brahmāyaṇī statue was re-enshrined back to her usual seat after the installation of finial (local resident, Maharjana, male, age 38).Three religious trusts in Thecva—Mū Guthi, Kvanā Guthi, and Nhesaḥ Guthi—are responsible for the worship, rituals, and festivals at the Brahmāyaṇī temple. The Mū Guthi and Nhesaḥ Guthi are managed by the Maharjanas, while the Kvanā Guthi is managed by the Mālīs. The members of these three trusts take turns performing daily worships at the temple on a monthly basis.The main festival in Thecva is the palanquin procession of Brahmāyaṇī and Bālakumārī. Brahmāyaṇī is considered the elder sister, and Bālakumārī is considered the younger sister. On the evening of the full moon day of Mārgaśīrṣa, the Brahmāyaṇī statue is brought down from the temple and cleaned. On this day, the Kvanā Guthi offerspañcabali, the sacrifice of five animals. Later, the Brahmāyaṇī statue is adorned with ornaments and taken to the Thecva Pīgaṃ (THE0110). The Bālakumārī palanquin is also brought there. Both palanquins are placed inside the sanctum of the Pīgaṃ, symbolizing a meeting between the sisters. On the following day, the 1st of the dark fortnight of Pauṣa, devotees throng the Pīgaṃ the entire day for the worship of the two deities, while also offering sacrifices and feasting. In the evening, Brahmāyaṇī and Bālakumārī are placed in their palanquins and paraded around Thecva.
description_ne: ग्वाः (गाई पालन गर्ने गोपाली) महिलाले निर्माण गरेको किम्बदन्ती रहेको ब्रह्मायणीको मन्दिर मध्यकालमै बनिसकेको कुरा अभिलेखले प्रमाणित गर्छ । मंसीर शुक्ल पूर्णिमा (यःमरि पुन्हि) देखि यी देवीको खटजात्रा शुरु हुन्छ ।थेच्वको क्वय्‌लाछि टोलमा ब्रह्मायणीको तल्ले शैलीको मन्दिर अवस्थित छ । दक्षिणाभिमुख गरी निर्माण गरिएको यस मन्दिरमा दुई तहको तामाको छाना राखिएको छ । छानामा सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको गजूर राखिएको छ । गजूरदेखि तल्लो छानासम्म पुग्ने गरी धातुको पताः झुण्ड्याइएको छ । मन्दिरको पहिलो तलामा सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएको ब्रह्मायणीको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ । मन्दिरको भुइँतलामा प्रवेशद्वारको पूर्वमा सानो कोठा बनाएर गणेशका मूर्तिहरू स्थापना गरिएका छन् । ती मूर्तिमध्ये आकृविहीन गणेश (THC0030-003) पुरानो र मुख्य मूर्ति हो । त्यसको पूर्वमा रहेको मूर्ति नयाँ हो । थेच्वका कुनै व्यक्ति जङ्गलमा दाउरा लिन जाँदा उनले फेला पारेका थिए । उनलाई गणेशले प्रत्यक्ष दर्शन दिएकोले उनले आफैले बोकेर ब्रह्मायणी मन्दिरमा स्थापना गरेका थिए भन्ने जनश्रुति रहेको छ । मन्दिरअगाडि राजहंस राखिएको ढुङ्गाको स्तम्भ ठड्याइएको छ । त्यस स्तम्भको दक्षिणमा डबली बनाइएको छ । जात्राको बेलामा ब्रह्मायणीको खट त्यसै डबलीमा राखिन्छ । थेच्वको नवदुर्गा नाच पनि यसै डबलीमा देखाइन्छ । सामान्यतया जमीनको सतहभन्दा केही माथि उठाएर डबली निर्माण गरिने भएपनि यहाँ जमीनको सतह र डबली एउटै सतहमा बनाइएको छ । मन्दिरबाहिर पूर्वपट्टि नासःद्यःको देवस्थल रहेको छयो मन्दिरको निर्माणसम्बन्धी कुनै अभिलेख प्राप्त भएको छैन, तर मध्यकालमै यो मन्दिर बनिसकेको कुरा अभिलेखले प्रमाणित गर्छ । किम्बदन्तीअनुसार यो मन्दिरको निर्माण ग्वाः (गाई पालन गर्ने गोपाली) महिलाले गरेको देखिन्छ । तीनजना ग्वाः दिदीबहिनीहरूको आपसी दुश्मनीको कारणले एकजनाले ग्वाःद्यः भनी गणेश स्थापना गरिन्, एकजनाले ब्रह्मायणी मन्दिर निर्माण गरिन्, अर्को एकजनाले ग्वाः ननिमा गणेश स्थापना गरेकी थिइन् । अर्को भनाइअनुसार दिदी ग्वाः महिलाले क्वय्‌लाछिमा ब्रह्मायणी स्थापना गरेकी थिइन् र बहिनीले च्वय्‌लाछिमा बालकुमारी स्थापना गरेकी थिइन् । नेसं ७५६ (सन् १६३६) मा कुलसिंह प्रमुख रहेको समूहले थेच्वमा नृत्यस्ठान (डबली) निर्माण गरेको थियो । नेसं ८२३ (सन् १७०२) मा थेच्वका थकालीहरू भारसिंह भावो र सूर्य भावोले गणेश (THC0030-002) स्थापना गरेका थिए । नेसं ८३७ (सन् १७१७) मा थेच्वमा बुद्धको भजन गाउने गुठीले क्वय्‌लाछि टोलमा रहेको चैत्य वरिपरि र ब्रह्मायणी मन्दिर अगाडिको खुल्ला ठाउँमा तेलिया इँटाले छापेको थियो । नेसं ८३७ (सन् १७१७) मा गुमीसिंह भावो, दातेम्ह भावो, इन्द्रसिं भावो लगायतका व्यक्तिहरूले मिलेर ब्रह्मायणीको लागि तीनवटा काष्ठतोरण चढाएका थिए । नेसं १०२१ (सन् १९०१) मा ब्रह्मायणी मन्दिरअगाडि राखिएको पुरानो काठको स्तम्भको ठाउँमा ढुङ्गाको स्तम्भ राखिएको थियो ।विसं २०७२ (सन् २०१५) को भूकम्पले मन्दिरमा क्षति पुगेको थियो । पुरातत्त्व विभागबाट मन्दिर पुनर्निर्माण गरिने भएपछि विसं २०७३ फागुन २९ गते आइतवार (सन् २०१७) देखि मन्दिर भत्काउन शुरु गरिएको थियो । त्यसैले मन्दिरको मुख्य देवता ब्रह्मायणीको मूर्तिलाई मन्दिरको पश्चि‍ममा रहेको सतःमा सारिएको थियो । मूर्तिलाई सतःमा राखिएको समयमै विसं २०७४ पौष १९ गते ब्रह्मायणीको मूर्ति चोरी भएको थियो (Local resident from a Maharjan caste, male, age 38) । त्यसभन्दा अघि पनि दुईपल्ट ब्रह्मायणीको मूर्ति चोरी भइसकेको थियो । चोरी भएका ब्रह्मायणीका कुनै पनि मूर्तिहरू फेला परेका छैनन् । त्यसैले स्थानीयहरूले मिलेर ब्रह्मायणीको नयाँ मूर्ति बनाएर स्थापना गरेका थिए । अहिले स्थापना गरिएको नयाँ मूर्ति ब्रह्मायणीको चौथो मूर्ति हो । विसं २०८१ मंसीर २१ गते शुक्रवार (सन् २०२४) मन्दिर पुनर्निर्माणको काम सम्पन्न भएर गजूर चढाई सतःमा राखिएको ब्रह्मायणीको मूर्तिलाई मन्दिरको गर्भगृहभित्र स्थापना गरिएको थियो (Local resident from a Maharjan caste, male, age 38) ।थेच्वमा रहेका विभिन्न गुठीमध्ये तीनवटा गुठी - मू गुठी, क्वना गुठी र न्हेसः गुठीले ब्रह्मायणी मन्दिरमा हुने पूजाआजा, जात्रा सञ्चालन गरिरहेको छ । मू गुठी र न्हेस गुठी महर्जनहरूले सञ्चालन गर्छन् भने क्वना गुठी चाहिँ मालीहरूले सञ्चालन गर्छन् । ती तीनवटा गुठीका गुठीयारहरूले एक-एक महिनाको पालो मिलाएर मन्दिरमा नित्यपूजा गरिरहेका छन् । थेच्वको मुख्य जात्रा ब्रह्मायणी र बालकुमारीको जात्रा हो । ब्रह्मायणीलाई दिदी र बालकुमारीलाई बहिनीको रूपमा लिइन्छ । जात्राको लागि मंसीर शुक्ल पूर्णिमा (यःमरि पुन्हि) को बेलुकी ब्रह्मायणीको मूर्तिलाई मन्दिरबाट तल ओरालेर सफा गरिन्छ । त्यस दिन क्वना गुठीको तर्फबाट पञ्चबलि दिइन्छ । त्यसपछि ब्रह्मायणीको मूर्तिलाई गरगहना लगाई थेच्व पीगं (THE0110) मा लगिन्छ । त्यहाँ बालकुमारीको खट पनि ल्याइएको हुन्छ । दुबै खटलाई पीगंको गर्भगृहभित्र राखिन्छ । त्यसलाई दिदीबहिनीको भेट भएको रूपमा लिइन्छ । भोलिपल्ट पौष कृष्ण प्रतिपदाको दिनमा दिनभरि ब्रह्मायणी र बालकुमारीको पूजा गरी बलि दिने, भोज खाने क्रम चलिरहन्छ । बेलुकी ब्रह्मायणी र बालकुमारीलाई खटमा राखेर थेच्वभरि परिक्रमा गराइन्छ ।

H: 36 cm, W: 25.5 cm. (D. Vajrācārya VS 2056, p. 74 has described the event as the establishment of Nāsaḥdyaḥ.)

historical_events.event_description: A group led by Kulasiṃha constructed a dance platform in Thecva. Other individuals like Doya Gvāra, Luṃgurāma, Jitalasiṃha, and Keśavacā were also involved in the construction.
Bhārasiṃha Bhābo and Sūrya Bhābo, seniors of Thecva, established a Gaṇeśa statue (THC0030-002).

A guild dedicated to chanting Buddhist hymns in Thecva paved the open space in front of the Brahmāyaṇī temple and the area around the Kvaylāchicaityawith floor tiles. The guild was led by Kṛṣṇadeva at the time with Viśvahari, Sūrjjarāma, Raghu, Siddhirāma, and others involved as members. The inscription recording this event bears a carving of acaityaon its upper portion. Thecaityamentioned in the inscription is Kvaylāchi Cībhāḥ (THC0130).
Gumīsiṃha Bhābo, Dātemha Bhābo, Indrasiṃ Bhābo, and others collectively donated three woodentoraṇas for Brahmāyaṇī.
Hākorāma Bhābo, Satyasiṃha Bhābo, Mohona Bhābo, and others jointly offered atoraṇato Brahmāyaṇī.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of a statue of shrew
historical_events.event_description: Suja Bhābo, Bābusiṃha Bhābo, Rāma Bhābo, and others made a collective offering of a stone statue of shrew, the animal mount of Gaṇeśa, for the Gaṇeśa enshrined in the Brahmāyaṇī temple.

historical_events.event_name: Replacing wooden pillar with stone pillar
historical_events.event_description: Hākusiṃ Bhābo of Nhesaḥ Guthi, Nekusiṃ Bhābo of Mū Guthi, Kṛṣṇasundara Mālī of Kvanā Guthi, and others jointly replaced the old wooden pillar in front of the Brahmāyaṇī temple with a stone pillar.

As the previous Gaṇeśa statue was in poor state, Jitāsiṃ Bhābo, Tulsī Bhābo, Nasiṃ Bhābo, Kīrtimāna Bhābo, and others offered a new statue. They also established a religious trust by donating land for the worship of Gaṇeśa on the 8th of the dark fortnight of Phālguna. Rājamāna Śākya was the artist who crafted the new statue.

The temple damaged by the 2015 earthquakes was reconstructed and the Brahmāyaṇī statue temporarily relocated to a nearbysataḥwas re-enshrined back to her usual seat in the temple after the installation of finial. The reconstruction was carried out by the Department of Archaeology.
